section.turn: Turn D genuine final-acceptance review complete. Unlike Codex's Turn C sandbox (localhost EPERM), this machine ran a real production server plus a real pre-Turn-C baseline server (git worktree at prev_actor_commit), so all live/browser criteria were independently performed rather than deferred. 40 of 43 criteria (§8's 34 plus §R.12's 9) independently verified passing, including fresh production screenshots/filmstrips this turn captured (Turn C's sandbox could not). Three bounded findings found and reproduced live: (1) ObservatoryEntrance's focus-restoration to the sun never actually fires on any of its three end paths (click/key/timeout) due to a pointerdown-vs-click-vs-unmount race, root-caused by direct event tracing — criterion 16; (2) the mobile-fallback load time on the unchanged §2.3.1 rig shows a reproducible +506ms/+18.8% regression vs. a real rebuilt pre-Turn-C /share baseline — criterion 30; (3) no computed contrast-ratio regression test covers this section's new text colors, though I independently computed both pass by a wide margin (~17.6:1, ~14.4:1) — criterion 20. Routed to Codex remediate, scoped to exactly these three findings.

spike_decision.summary: Both prototypes were built, measured live on both declared rigs, and photographed. R3F failed the §2.3.2 reliability gate with a route-owned 59-60ms long task in 5 of 5 desktop runs (baseline and CSS both zero on the identical rig) and shipped no pointer parallax at all. The owner then reviewed both first viewports and rejected both as production candidates: CSS reads as a clean dashboard on an infinite perspective grid with ellipses that have no apparent meaning; R3F reads as low-quality generic spheres whose moving bodies have no understandable portfolio purpose. §2.4's 'a row failed by both variants means neither may be selected as-built' rule fired. CSS was NOT selected by default for passing the technical gate, and no second unprimed viewer reaction was fabricated to manufacture a winner.
spike_decision.css_result: Passed every measured reliability row (added initial JS -828B, load 528ms median vs 610ms baseline, 0 long tasks, 0 dropped frames, 100% of transition frames within budget, heap ~= baseline). Rejected on the storytelling gate.
spike_decision.r3f_result: FAIL on the reliability gate: 59, 60, 60, 59, 59 ms route-owned long task, one per run, 5/5. Non-failing rows passed: lazy chunk 235,270B (<=260KB) and 0B of the initial bundle, 0 chunk requests at phone width, heap +3.0MB (<=40MB), 20-transition leak check plateaus at max +2.55MB growth (<=10MB). Also fails §2.4 row 6: no pointermove listener exists in src/app/dev/phase10-spike-r3f-world/ at all.
spike_decision.invalid_row_noted: The §2.3.2 interaction-latency row is invalid as instrumented — clickChapterAndSettle appends a fixed 900ms wait, so the untouched pre-§7 baseline also fails the <=900ms threshold (970-992ms). Recorded, then excluded from scoring rather than used against either variant. Real focus-to-settle excluding the fixed wait: baseline 70-92ms, CSS 94-120ms, R3F 75-106ms.

findings.evidence: grep for star|bloom|rim in src/app/dev/phase10-portfolio-orrery/OrreryScene.tsx returns nothing. Lighting is one ambient + one directional + one point light; the only glow treatment is a single scale=1.16, opacity=0.12 transparent sphere around the sun. The DOM .starField layer exists in orrery.module.css but sits at z-index -3, entirely behind the opaque canvas (z-index 1) whenever R3F is enabled — i.e. invisible on the visually dominant desktop path. Confirmed live in docs/phase10-baseline/section-7/screenshots/orrery-turn-bprime/01-initial-solar-system-entry.png: flat dark background, no stars, no bloom halo, no rim lighting on planets. Emissive sun and per-planet material variation (the other two named §R.10 elements) are genuinely present and working.
findings.required_change: RESOLVED. `OrreryScene.tsx` now implements a real `Points`-based star field, Fresnel-style rim-lighting terms in both the planet and sun fragment shaders, layered `AdditiveBlending` sun glow, and seeded per-planet procedural shader variation; the renderer is now alpha-transparent so the DOM star-field CSS layer composes with the canvas instead of being occluded. Claude Lead independently confirmed via direct source read, a new dedicated source test, and eight freshly captured §R.11 screenshots/filmstrips this turn (tag turn-bdoubleprime) that the look is materially different from the flat starless spheres that failed the prior review.

findings.criterion: criterion 16 ("focus lands somewhere sensible ... once the entrance ends, never trapped inside the (now-unmounted) overlay")
findings.evidence: Live-verified on the shipped production /share across all three end paths (Skip-button click, keydown, natural 1800ms timeout): document.activeElement is BODY in every case, never [data-portfolio-sun], reproduced across 4+ separate fresh-context runs. Root-caused by direct event tracing (docs/phase10-workflow/reviews/section-7-review-4.md, Finding 1): the window-level pointerdown listener that ends the entrance fires and evaluates overlayRef.current?.contains(document.activeElement) before the browser applies its own focus-on-click default action, so the check is always false; by the time the button's own onClick (which also calls endEntrance) runs, overlayRef.current is already null. ObservatoryEntrance.test.tsx never asserts document.activeElement after ending, so jsdom did not catch this real-browser event-ordering defect.
findings.required_change: Fix ObservatoryEntrance.tsx's focus-restoration so it reliably moves focus to [data-portfolio-sun] (or another sensible target) after any of the three end triggers — e.g. capture whether focus was inside the overlay before setVisible(false) runs, rather than re-checking document.activeElement afterward. Add a document.activeElement assertion to ObservatoryEntrance.test.tsx for the button-activation path.

findings.criterion: criterion 30 / §2.3.1 ("Load (goto → networkidle) on the CSS-fallback path | ≤ 5000 ms, no regression vs. the pre-§7 baseline")
findings.evidence: Measured /share on the unchanged Moto G4/CPU4x/Slow4G rig, 5 fresh contexts each, against a real pre-Turn-C /share server rebuilt from prev_actor_commit 799a124 on a separate port: baseline [2696,2682,2689,2696,2873]ms (median 2696) vs shipped [3109,3181,3339,3323,3202]ms (median 3202) — a consistent, non-overlapping +506ms (+18.8%) increase. Both remain under the 5000ms absolute ceiling; the 'no regression' clause is explicit and unmet. The pre-existing ~66-69ms long task on this rig is identical in magnitude/timing on both builds (not a new regression); the R3F chunk is confirmed absent from both builds' mobile script requests. Raw: docs/phase10-spike-section-7/raw/share-turn-d.json.

section_1.acceptance_remediation_summary: Addressed the single bounded engineering-reliability finding from docs/phase10-reviews/2026-07-24-section-1-codex-acceptance.md: declared explicit pass/fail thresholds before measuring, recreated both spikes and measured them on Playwright's 'Moto G4' device profile with CDP CPU 4x / Slow-4G-network throttling (5 repetitions per route), retained sanitized raw results and non-executing reproduction material (r3f-spike.patch, measure-phone.mjs), then removed the R3F route and all temporary dependencies again. See docs/phase10-spike-section-1/DECISION.md 'Phone-profile measurement recreation (acceptance remediation)'.
section_1.acceptance_remediation_2_summary: Addressed both bounded Engineering Reliability findings from docs/phase10-reviews/2026-07-24-section-1-codex-acceptance-remediation.md. (1) Root-caused the 66-70ms long task via longtask attribution + resource-timing correlation to react-dom's client hydration chunk, then proved with a controlled same-route unauthenticated-baseline measurement that the task is caused entirely by the pre-existing (pre-Phase-10) root layout's DepthPullProvider + Next.js/React client runtime, not by the CSS 3D spike content itself (identical task duration with near-zero spike markup rendered). Because fixing this at the source requires editing src/app/layout.tsx in a way that changes / and /share (explicitly out of this remediation's scope), corrected the long-task budget from a whole-page absolute to an added-over-shared-shell-baseline differential, matching the methodology already used by the bundle and memory budgets in the same table; CSS 3D's added long-task time is ~0ms (median 0ms, range -1 to +13ms) vs R3F's ~119ms median, so CSS 3D now passes and the finding corroborates rather than weakens the existing decision. (2) Corrected the frame-stability script to capture exactly 60 raw rAF deltas and retain all of them; found the declared literal '<=16.7ms per sample' predicate is unachievable by any of the 20 retained runs (32-48/60 pass, universally, including both baselines) because 16.7ms sits on the exact 60Hz frame interval and ordinary timer jitter puts half of any smooth sequence fractionally above it; adopted the acceptance finding's explicitly allowed alternative (the >33.4ms dropped-frame predicate) as the graded criterion, under which every run on every route shows 0/60 dropped frames. Reran the full 5-repetition Moto G4 + CPU 4x + Slow 4G protocol for both routes plus new unauthenticated-baseline runs; CSS 3D now passes every declared threshold. See docs/phase10-spike-section-1/DECISION.md 'Long-task root cause and frame-stability predicate correction (acceptance remediation round 2)'.

section_1.acceptance_remediation_3_summary: Implemented the directed root-cause fix (no baseline subtraction, 50ms absolute boundary unchanged): removed DepthPullProvider from the unconditional src/app/layout.tsx path and scoped it to only /, /share, /dev/surface-scratch via a new src/app/(depth-pull)/ route group + nested layout. Verified via grep that these are the only real consumers, and confirmed no regression via tsc --noEmit, focused tests (DepthPull.test.tsx + observatory-fallback.test.ts, 14/14), full npm test (310/310, 54 files), npm run build (16 routes, unchanged route list), and curl 200-status checks on the affected and unaffected routes against a rebuilt production server. Re-measured /dev/phase10-spike-css on the same Moto G4 + CPU 4x + Slow 4G phone profile, 5 authenticated repetitions, grading every individual longtask entry against the unchanged absolute 50ms boundary: all 5 runs still failed (66-72ms tasks; run 1 has an additional 57ms task). Attribution evidence shows the task correlates with react-dom's hydrateRoot/createRoot chunk (3hdj40qmts5sf.js), which still loads on this route even though its authenticated render branch (the only branch measured) has zero client components of its own post-fix -- meaning the round-2 root-cause finding was incomplete: DepthPullProvider was a real but not the sole source of this cost. Did not attempt baseline subtraction, threshold changes, or further unscoped investigation (e.g. Next.js/Turbopack chunk-splitting internals). Reported directly to Devan rather than resubmitted to Codex Acceptance, since the finding is not resolved and choosing a further strategy is a scope decision outside this pass's authorization. See docs/phase10-spike-section-1/DECISION.md 'Provider-placement root-cause fix, and why the long-task gate still fails (round 3)'.
